    AI Overview
    Peter Alexander is leaving NBC News after 22 years to join MS NOW (formerly MSNBC) as an anchor and chief national reporter, starting in 2026. He will anchor a new weekday program and aims to spend more time with his family after serving as NBC's chief White House correspondent. 
    Key Details of the Move: 
    • New Role: Alexander will anchor the 11 a.m. Eastern hour on MS NOW and serve as a chief national reporter.
    • Departure from NBC: He is leaving his roles as NBC News chief White House correspondent and co-host of Saturday Today.
    • Reason for Leaving: Alexander cited a desire to "challenge himself with something new" and to spend more time with his children, as noted by his co-host Laura Jarrett on Today.
    • Timing: The move follows the 2025 separation of MSNBC (now MS NOW) from NBC, with Alexander being a significant talent crossover. 
    He leaves with high praise from NBC leadership, including Washington Bureau Chief Chloe Arensberg.
